item.title: Counterpoint and what comes after
item.content:encoded:
Now that Counterpoint has been posted and wrapped up the first suite of tales for this canon, I wanted to formally invite others to contribute. I'm going to (try to) take a break from "On Mount Golgotha" tales for a bit - partly to recharge, and partly because me writing too much damages the collaborative nature of the canon.

I wanted to post here to throw out some ideas for where the story could go next, in case people are looking for inspiration. Spoilers aplenty under both collapsibles.

+ Ideas for tales / character developments
– hide block

This is not intended to be limiting in any way - more a starting point in case people want one.

  • My aim in ending "Counterpoint" like I did was to get Emma (and the story) out into the world, and move off-site (where most of the existing stories have been set). The story could easily be a quest narrative - several different items (SCP-012, the other scores, Pherson) to collect, and a bigger mystery to uncover.
  • Remember, Emma is a site-baby, so how does she react to going out into the world to lead an MTF?
  • In A Convincing Lyre, Emma mentioned having a brother with otitis. But if she was a site-baby, so was he - is he still with the Foundation? If so, could he be a candidate to join Eta-11?
  • What does the MTF think of Emma being put in charge? What does it do to her friendship with Mike?
  • How does Richards' arrest affect Dee, who owes him a great deal, but already has trust issues? How does Dee take to working for Emma?
  • What does Roger feel about being a field agent again? Has he got a history with Hennessey, or the other older members of Eta-11?
  • Who was Pherson co-operating with when he brazenly stole the baton?
  • Emma knows that Alagadda is involved with 012. Is it worth her interviewing Dr. Narváez from SCP-2264?
  • For a one-shot, you could tell the story of the Renaissance composer who was found buried in the church in The Journal of K.M. Sandoval. Who was his masked patron? Is there an Alagadda connection?
  • Emma says early on that she isn't good at music, but she wrote some that she gave to ProfetiX in Pattern Breaker - what did she mean when she said that she wasn't good?
  • Amnestics play an interesting role in the canon. Roger overdosed on them, Rita was rendered immune to them in Bigger Than Jesus, Mace mentions in Dreams of Failure that they didn't work properly for him. Something to follow up?

+ Larger canon mysteries where WJS or I can provide guidance
– hide block

If you are looking to link things into the end-game of the On Mount Golgotha storyline, you might need to know what we have in mind, so feel free to get in touch. Below are some things where we can help you keep consistent - WJS might have more to add:

  • We have an idea of what SCP-012 does when it is played in full.
  • We know what Saint Alagadda is and its purpose.
  • I have some definite ideas about the "other scores" referred to in Pattern Breaker, although not all of the details are settled.
  • The imagery in Our Mutual Guide is important, and I can explain all of the references if required.
  • I don't have a strong view on where SCP-012 is being hidden. Happy for it to be a McGuffin, or for it to be recovered.

item.title: Re: A thought just struck me
item.content:encoded:
To flip the perspective, its really harmony, uniformity, and completeness that are the flawed concepts. Art's a wild creature- the cacaphonic noise of unbridled creation is where it thrives.

Like Pete Townshend put it: The distortion becomes somehow pure in its wildness.

item.title: A thought just struck me
item.content:encoded:
SCP-012 can be read as an allegory for the wiki itself:

  • many authors come together over time to create it
  • they pour out their creative life-force to bring it into existence
  • each makes their individual contribution, but towards a single core concept
  • the result is not uniform or even harmonious - a cacophony of canons
  • in the bigger picture, all their efforts are doomed, as it will never be "finished"

Perhaps that echo of experience found in On Mount Golgotha, by many a prospective author pouring their heart into their work only to die upon posting, is part of the source of its power.
